items.title: The discount is written into the caller's cart and compounds
items.hit: Says computeTotal assigns to item.price in the cart it was given, so a second call (renderSummary runs on every cart update) discounts again, or the summary lines show the mutated prices.
items.partial: Notes that the function mutates its argument without the repeated-call or displayed-price consequence.

items.title: Free shipping is now decided on the discounted amount
items.hit: Says that without a coupon the subtotal is accumulated from discounted prices, so the free-shipping threshold (and the reported subtotal) uses the amount after the loyalty discount, against 'decided on the subtotal before any discount'.
items.partial: Says the reported subtotal changed for loyal customers without mentioning shipping.

items.title: A customer with exactly five orders gets no discount
items.hit: Says `completedOrders > LOYALTY_MIN_ORDERS` excludes five, against 'five or more'.

items.title: The loyalty cache is unnecessary and goes stale
items.hit: Says the Map in loyalty.js caches two comparisons, is never invalidated, and keeps a customer's first answer after their order count or staff flag changes; or recommends removing it for either reason.
items.partial: Questions the cache without the staleness consequence or a removal recommendation.

items.title: skipLoyalty and loyaltyApplied serve no requirement
items.hit: Says no caller passes options.skipLoyalty, or nothing reads loyaltyApplied, and no requirement asks for either.

items.title: One rule is implemented twice and woven into the subtotal
items.hit: Says the loyalty discount has two implementations (per-item price before the subtotal without a coupon, on the discounted amount with one) or that it is interleaved with subtotal accumulation, AND proposes one step after the coupon that leaves the subtotal as it was.
items.partial: Calls the function hard to follow, or notes the repeated 0.95, without the two-path observation or the single-step proposal.

items.title: The tests pin the wrong numbers and miss every failing scenario
items.hit: Names at least one concrete regression the tests let through: a second call on the same cart, free shipping at the threshold for a loyal customer, exactly five orders, a coupon together with the discount; or says the loyal-customer test asserts the discounted subtotal as expected.
items.partial: Asks for more tests without naming a scenario.

items.title: A discount framework
items.violated: Recommends a rules engine, a strategy or pipeline of discount objects, or configuration-driven discounts for this change. Named steps or functions inside the module are not a violation.

items.title: Replacing float arithmetic
items.violated: Recommends, as a finding against this change, moving money to integer cents or a decimal library. The base already computes in floats with round2; a remark about the per-item rounding the change introduces is not a violation.
